lessons.title: Notre école dans la communauté
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify their school as an important part of their local autumn community

opening.activity: Community circle where students look out classroom windows and share what they see in their school neighborhood. Introduce the word 'communauté' with wide arm gestures showing connection.
opening.visualSupports: Wide arm gestures for community, pointing outward for neighborhood, heart hands for belonging

main.activity: School community exploration using school maps and autumn neighborhood photos. Students create a 'Our School Community' poster, drawing or pasting pictures of places and people they see around school in autumn. Emphasize how school connects to neighborhood.
main.visualSupports: Connecting gestures between school and community, proud posture for school belonging, discovery expressions

decisionPoints.question: How familiar are students with the area around their school?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage students to share specific places they know and visit with families
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use photos and maps to introduce nearby community places and explain connections

decisionPoints.question: What community landmarks can students see from school windows?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Point out visible landmarks and explain how they connect to school community
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use photos of nearby landmarks and discuss how they support school community

closing.activity: Community belonging circle where students share one thing they like about their school being part of the community. End with group chant: 'Notre école fait partie de notre communauté!'

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students not understanding how school connects to community
troubleshooting.then: Use concrete examples like mail delivery to school, school buses in neighborhood, families walking to school

lessons.realWorldConnection: Our school is connected to many community helpers and neighbors who work together in autumn

lessons.title: Les personnes qui nous aident à l'école
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize the school community helpers who support their learning every day

opening.activity: Helper appreciation circle where students think of one school person who helps them. Practice helper appreciation gestures and the phrase 'Merci de nous aider!'
opening.visualSupports: Helping hands gestures, grateful expressions, pointing to helper photos with appreciation

main.activity: School helper exploration using photos and possible mini-interviews. Students create a 'School Helpers' book with drawings and simple descriptions of what each helper does. Include principal, secretary, custodian, librarian, and volunteers.
main.visualSupports: Helper-specific gestures (key for principal, cleaning for custodian), appreciation expressions, helping hand motions

decisionPoints.question: Which school helpers do students interact with most often?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on these familiar helpers first and add others as extensions
decisionPoints.ifNo: Introduce helpers through photos and explain how they help students even if not seen daily

decisionPoints.question: Should we include volunteers or focus only on staff?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include parent volunteers and reading helpers to show broader school community
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on consistent staff helpers that students see regularly

closing.activity: Helper appreciation circle where students share which school helper they'd like to thank and why. Practice saying 'Merci' to different school helpers they might see.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students not recognizing less visible school helpers
troubleshooting.then: Take brief school walk to see helpers at work or arrange brief helper visits to classroom

lessons.realWorldConnection: Many people work together to make our school a safe, clean, and welcoming place to learn

lessons.title: Les changements d'automne dans notre communauté
lessons.oneGoal: Students will observe and describe how autumn brings changes to their local community

opening.activity: Autumn observation circle where students share autumn changes they've noticed at home or school. Practice autumn vocabulary with seasonal gestures and expressions.
opening.visualSupports: Falling leaf gestures, cooler weather motions (rubbing arms), changing colors hand movements

main.activity: Community autumn changes exploration using before/after photos of local areas in summer vs autumn. Students create an 'Autumn Changes' observation journal, drawing community changes they see and describing them with simple French words.
main.visualSupports: Comparison gestures (showing different), observation motions (pointing and looking), seasonal change expressions

decisionPoints.question: What autumn changes are most visible in our local area?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on dramatic local changes like leaf colors, harvest activities, or weather preparations
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use photos of typical autumn changes and help students look for subtle local changes

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on natural changes or community activity changes?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Balance both natural changes (leaves, weather) and community changes (harvest festivals, preparation activities)
decisionPoints.ifNo: Start with natural changes students can see, then connect to community activity changes

closing.activity: Autumn appreciation circle where students share their favorite autumn change in the community. Practice saying 'J'aime l'automne parce que...'

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students not noticing community changes beyond obvious leaf colors
troubleshooting.then: Provide specific prompts: people's clothing, community decorations, different activities outside

lessons.realWorldConnection: Autumn brings special changes that affect how our community looks, feels, and works together

lessons.title: Les gens qui nous gardent en sécurité
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify community safety helpers and understand how they protect everyone in autumn

opening.activity: Safety helper circle where students share safety helpers they know. Practice safety vocabulary with protective gestures and expressions of gratitude for safety helpers.
opening.visualSupports: Protective gestures (shield motion), safety pointing (stop hand), grateful expressions for helpers

main.activity: Safety helper exploration using photos and simple role-play. Students create a 'Safety Helpers' chart showing different helpers (police, firefighters, crossing guards) and how they keep the community safe in autumn weather.
main.visualSupports: Helper-specific gestures (traffic directing for crossing guard, siren sounds for emergency helpers), safety expressions

decisionPoints.question: Are students comfortable discussing safety without creating fear?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on positive safety helper roles and how they help community feel secure
decisionPoints.ifNo: Emphasize helper friendliness and community service rather than emergency situations

decisionPoints.question: Which safety helpers are most visible in our community?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Feature most visible helpers prominently and explain their daily community presence
decisionPoints.ifNo: Introduce variety of safety helpers and explain when and how they help community

closing.activity: Safety appreciation circle where students practice saying 'Merci de nous protéger' and share how safety helpers make them feel secure in their community.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students feeling anxious about safety topics
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize helper friendliness, community care, and how helpers prevent problems rather than respond to emergencies

lessons.realWorldConnection: Safety helpers work every day, including during autumn, to keep our community safe and secure

lessons.title: Visite d'un pompier à l'école
lessons.oneGoal: Students will learn about fire safety and fire fighters' important community role through a special visit

opening.activity: Fire safety preparation circle where students practice fire safety vocabulary and prepare respectful questions for firefighter visitor. Review appropriate visitor behavior.
opening.visualSupports: Fire safety gestures (stop drop roll motions), respectful listening posture, question asking gestures

main.activity: Firefighter visit (or virtual presentation) with Q&A, equipment demonstration, and fire safety education. Students create a 'Fire Safety' reminder poster with key safety messages and appreciation for firefighters.
main.visualSupports: Following firefighter demonstrations, safety rule gestures, appreciation expressions for visitor

decisionPoints.question: Can we arrange an actual firefighter visit or should we use virtual resources?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Coordinate with local fire department for in-person visit with equipment demonstration
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use high-quality virtual firefighter presentation with interactive elements and Q&A

decisionPoints.question: What fire safety concepts are appropriate for Grade 1?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on basic safety: stop-drop-roll, calling 911, meeting spots, not playing with fire
decisionPoints.ifNo: Keep concepts simple and positive, focusing on firefighter helpers rather than fire dangers

closing.activity: Firefighter appreciation circle where students share what they learned and practice saying 'Merci, pompier!' End with commitment to fire safety rules.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students becoming too excited or distracted during firefighter visit
troubleshooting.then: Use structured Q&A format, clear expectations, and frequent appreciation reminders to maintain focus

lessons.realWorldConnection: Fire fighters help our community stay safe from fires and other emergencies all year long

lessons.title: Les gens qui nous aident quand nous sommes malades
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand how healthcare helpers support community wellness in all seasons

opening.activity: Health helper circle where students share healthcare helpers they know (doctors, nurses, dentists). Practice health vocabulary with caring gestures and wellness expressions.
opening.visualSupports: Caring gestures (gentle hands), health checking motions (listening, looking), wellness expressions

main.activity: Healthcare helper exploration using photos and simple health role-play. Students create a 'Health Helpers' book showing different helpers and how they keep the community healthy, especially during autumn cold season.
main.visualSupports: Helper-specific gestures (stethoscope listening, gentle care motions), health and wellness expressions

decisionPoints.question: Should we include mental health helpers or focus on physical health?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include school counselors and explain how they help with feelings and worries
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on familiar physical health helpers that students encounter regularly

decisionPoints.question: How do we discuss medical help without creating anxiety?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Emphasize helper kindness, community care, and how helpers help people feel better
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on wellness promotion and helper friendliness rather than illness treatment

closing.activity: Health appreciation circle where students share ways to stay healthy and practice thanking healthcare helpers with 'Merci de prendre soin de nous!'

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students feeling worried about medical situations
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize prevention, wellness, and helper kindness; focus on how helpers help people feel better and stronger

lessons.realWorldConnection: Healthcare helpers work to keep everyone in our community healthy and strong

lessons.title: Les gens qui apportent notre nourriture
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore how food gets to their community and the helpers involved in this process

opening.activity: Food journey circle where students think about where their breakfast came from. Practice food helper vocabulary with farm-to-table gestures and appreciation expressions.
opening.visualSupports: Farm growing gestures, transportation motions, food sharing expressions, grateful eating motions

main.activity: Food system exploration using autumn harvest photos and food journey maps. Students create a 'From Farm to Table' poster showing farmers, truckers, store workers, and how autumn harvest reaches their community.
main.visualSupports: Sequential gestures for food journey, harvest celebration motions, food sharing expressions

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on local farmers or include broader food supply chain?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Emphasize local autumn harvest and nearby farms that supply community stores
decisionPoints.ifNo: Include broader food system while highlighting autumn harvest and seasonal foods

decisionPoints.question: Which food helpers are most visible in our autumn community?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Feature farmers market vendors, grocery store workers, and autumn harvest helpers
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use photos to introduce variety of food system workers and their autumn contributions

closing.activity: Food appreciation circle where students share their favorite autumn food and practice saying 'Merci aux fermiers!' for bringing food to community.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students not understanding food journey from farm to home
troubleshooting.then: Use specific examples with familiar foods, simple sequential pictures, and concrete farm-to-store connections

lessons.realWorldConnection: Many helpers work together to bring fresh, healthy food to our community, especially during autumn harvest

lessons.title: Visite à l'épicerie du quartier
lessons.oneGoal: Students will observe food helpers in action and understand the grocery store as a community hub

opening.activity: Grocery store preparation circle where students practice grocery vocabulary and prepare respectful observation questions. Review field trip behavior expectations.
opening.visualSupports: Shopping gestures, respectful observation postures, polite interaction expressions

main.activity: Grocery store field trip (or virtual tour) observing workers, autumn produce, and community interactions. Students complete observation checklist and practice polite interactions with store helpers.
materials: field trip permission or virtual tour
main.visualSupports: Following field trip guides, observation gestures, polite interaction demonstrations

decisionPoints.question: Can we arrange an actual grocery store field trip or virtual tour?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Coordinate with local grocery store for educational visit with worker interactions
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use comprehensive virtual grocery tour with focus on worker roles and community service

decisionPoints.question: Which grocery store roles should we highlight for Grade 1?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on visible roles: cashiers, produce workers, managers, cart helpers
decisionPoints.ifNo: Introduce variety of store workers and explain how they serve community families

closing.activity: Grocery appreciation circle where students share what they observed and practice thanking store workers with 'Merci de nous servir!'

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students getting overwhelmed or distracted during field trip
troubleshooting.then: Use buddy system, clear observation focus, and frequent appreciation reminders to maintain educational purpose

lessons.realWorldConnection: Grocery stores are important community places where food helpers serve families every day

lessons.title: Les gens qui gardent notre communauté propre
lessons.oneGoal: Students will appreciate sanitation workers and understand how keeping communities clean is everyone's job

opening.activity: Clean community circle where students share what they do to keep spaces clean. Practice cleanliness vocabulary with tidy-up gestures and environmental appreciation.
opening.visualSupports: Cleaning gestures (sweeping, picking up), environmental care motions, pride in clean spaces expressions

main.activity: Environmental helper exploration using photos of sanitation workers, recycling helpers, and park maintenance. Students create a 'Clean Community' action plan showing how helpers and families work together, especially with autumn leaf cleanup.
main.visualSupports: Environmental helper gestures, recycling motions, community cooperation expressions

decisionPoints.question: Should we include environmental helpers beyond garbage collection?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include park maintenance, recycling workers, and environmental protection helpers
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on most visible sanitation workers and explain their daily community contributions

decisionPoints.question: How do we emphasize student responsibility for community cleanliness?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Balance helper appreciation with student actions like not littering and helping with cleanup
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus primarily on helper appreciation while mentioning simple student contributions

closing.activity: Clean community commitment circle where students share one way they'll help keep their community clean and practice saying 'Merci de garder notre communauté propre!'

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students not understanding connection between individual actions and community cleanliness
troubleshooting.then: Use concrete examples of how one person's littering affects everyone, and how helping cleanup benefits whole community

lessons.realWorldConnection: Keeping our community clean requires helpers working together and everyone doing their part

lessons.title: Les activités d'automne dans notre communauté
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify special autumn activities that bring their community together

opening.activity: Autumn activity circle where students share autumn activities they enjoy with families. Practice autumn celebration vocabulary with festive gestures and community expressions.
opening.visualSupports: Celebration gestures (clapping, cheering), autumn activity motions, community togetherness expressions

main.activity: Community autumn celebration exploration using local event photos and activity descriptions. Students create an 'Autumn Community Calendar' showing harvest festivals, Halloween events, and autumn sports that bring neighbors together.
main.visualSupports: Activity-specific gestures, calendar organization motions, community participation expressions

decisionPoints.question: Which autumn activities are most common in our local community?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Feature prominent local events like harvest festivals, pumpkin patches, or autumn sports
decisionPoints.ifNo: Introduce variety of typical autumn community activities and help students identify local versions

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on organized events or informal community gatherings?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include both formal events and informal activities like neighborhood leaf raking or outdoor play
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on organized community events that families can easily participate in together

closing.activity: Autumn celebration circle where students share which community autumn activity they'd most like to try and practice saying 'J'aimerais participer!'

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students not aware of local community autumn activities
troubleshooting.then: Provide specific local examples, send home family inquiry about autumn activities, use photos of nearby events

lessons.realWorldConnection: Autumn brings special opportunities for community members to celebrate and have fun together

lessons.title: Promenade dans le quartier en automne
lessons.oneGoal: Students will observe their neighborhood community helpers and autumn changes through direct exploration

opening.activity: Neighborhood walk preparation circle where students practice observation vocabulary and prepare safety rules for community exploration. Review respectful neighbor behavior.
opening.visualSupports: Observation gestures (pointing, looking carefully), safety rule demonstrations, respectful neighbor interactions

main.activity: Neighborhood walk (or virtual neighborhood tour) observing autumn changes, community helpers at work, and neighborhood helpers. Students complete neighborhood observation journal documenting helpers and autumn changes they discover.
materials: neighborhood walk route or virtual tour
main.visualSupports: Guided observation techniques, discovery expressions, community helper identification gestures

decisionPoints.question: Can we take an actual neighborhood walk or should we use virtual exploration?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Plan safe walking route with multiple helper observation opportunities and autumn change viewing
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use comprehensive virtual neighborhood tour with interactive elements and discussion opportunities

decisionPoints.question: Which community helpers are we likely to see during our walk?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Prepare students to recognize mail carriers, crossing guards, maintenance workers, shop keepers
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use photos and descriptions to supplement observation with helper identification activities

closing.activity: Neighborhood discovery circle where students share their most interesting observation and practice saying 'J'ai découvert que...'

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students having difficulty focusing observation during walk
troubleshooting.then: Use specific observation prompts, buddy observation system, and frequent stop-and-share opportunities

lessons.realWorldConnection: Taking time to really look at our neighborhood helps us appreciate all the helpers around us

lessons.title: Les gens qui nous aident à nous déplacer
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore transportation helpers who keep community members moving safely

opening.activity: Transportation circle where students share how they get to school and around community. Practice transportation vocabulary with movement gestures and safety expressions.
opening.visualSupports: Transportation motions (driving, walking, riding), safety rule gestures, grateful traveler expressions

main.activity: Transportation helper exploration using photos of bus drivers, crossing guards, traffic officers, and road maintenance workers. Students create a 'Safe Transportation' poster showing helpers who keep community members moving safely in autumn weather.
main.visualSupports: Helper-specific motions, safety demonstration gestures, weather-appropriate transportation expressions

decisionPoints.question: Should we include public transportation or focus on school transportation?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include both school buses and public transportation to show full range of community transportation
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on school transportation helpers that students interact with most regularly

decisionPoints.question: Which transportation helpers are most relevant to student experience?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Emphasize school bus drivers, crossing guards, and walking safety helpers
decisionPoints.ifNo: Introduce variety of transportation helpers and explain how they serve different community needs

closing.activity: Transportation appreciation circle where students practice thanking transportation helpers with 'Merci de nous aider à voyager en sécurité!'

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students not recognizing less visible transportation helpers
troubleshooting.then: Point out specific helpers during school arrival/dismissal, use photos of helpers at work, explain helper importance

lessons.realWorldConnection: Transportation helpers make it possible for people to move safely around our community

lessons.title: Les gens qui construisent et réparent
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand how construction and repair workers maintain and improve their community

opening.activity: Building and repair circle where students share things that need fixing or building in their community. Practice construction vocabulary with building gestures and improvement expressions.
opening.visualSupports: Building motions (hammering, measuring), repair gestures, community improvement expressions

main.activity: Construction helper exploration using photos of builders, repair workers, road crews, and maintenance teams. Students create a 'Community Builders' appreciation chart showing how these helpers make community stronger, especially preparing for autumn and winter.
main.visualSupports: Construction motions, seasonal preparation gestures, community strength expressions

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on new construction or maintenance and repair work?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Balance both new building projects and ongoing maintenance that keeps community functioning
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on maintenance and repair work that students can observe in their daily community experience

decisionPoints.question: Which construction helpers are most visible in our autumn community?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Highlight road crews, building maintenance, and autumn preparation workers
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use photos to introduce variety of construction helpers and explain their community contributions

closing.activity: Builder appreciation circle where students share how construction helpers make their community better and practice saying 'Merci de construire notre communauté!'

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students not understanding connection between construction work and community improvement
troubleshooting.then: Use before/after photos of community improvements, point out specific construction benefits for families

lessons.realWorldConnection: Construction and repair workers help make our community stronger and better for everyone

lessons.title: Comment nous pouvons aider notre communauté
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify ways they can contribute to their community as young citizens

opening.activity: Young helper circle where students share ways they already help at home or school. Practice citizen vocabulary with helpful gestures and community contribution expressions.
opening.visualSupports: Helping hand gestures, citizen pride expressions, community contribution motions

main.activity: Young citizen exploration using photos of children helping community and age-appropriate service ideas. Students create a 'Young Citizens' action plan showing realistic ways Grade 1 students can contribute to community wellbeing.
main.visualSupports: Service action demonstrations, citizen pride gestures, community impact expressions

decisionPoints.question: What are realistic ways Grade 1 students can help their community?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on simple actions: not littering, being kind to neighbors, helping elderly, thanking helpers
decisionPoints.ifNo: Brainstorm with students and provide examples of age-appropriate community contributions

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on individual actions or group community projects?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include both individual kindness actions and simple group projects like card-making for helpers
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on individual actions students can take immediately in their daily community interactions

closing.activity: Young citizen commitment circle where students choose one way they'll help their community and practice saying 'Je vais aider ma communauté en...'

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students feeling too young to make a community difference
troubleshooting.then: Provide specific examples of young people helping, emphasize that small actions matter, build confidence about impact

lessons.realWorldConnection: Even young people can make important contributions to help their community be better

lessons.title: Créer une carte de notre communauté
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create a visual map showing important community helpers and places in their neighborhood

opening.activity: Map-making circle where students share places they know in their community. Practice mapping vocabulary with directional gestures and location expressions.
opening.visualSupports: Directional pointing, map-reading gestures, location identification expressions

main.activity: Community map creation using simple base maps or drawing from scratch. Students add community helper locations, important places, and autumn features to create personalized community maps showing where helpers work and families visit.
main.visualSupports: Map-making motions, spatial organization gestures, community pride expressions

decisionPoints.question: Should maps focus on helper locations or general community landmarks?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Balance both helper workplaces and general landmarks to show complete community picture
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on helper locations while including key landmarks that students recognize

decisionPoints.question: What map-making tools are appropriate for Grade 1 students?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use simple symbols, stickers, and drawing tools that allow creative but clear map-making
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide templates with some pre-drawn elements that students can add to and personalize

closing.activity: Map sharing circle where students show their community maps and practice describing locations with 'Sur ma carte, je vois...'

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students having difficulty representing spatial relationships on maps
troubleshooting.then: Use concrete reference points, provide map templates with major landmarks, focus on general location rather than precise mapping

lessons.realWorldConnection: Making maps helps us understand how our community is organized and where helpers work

lessons.title: Dessiner nos héros communautaires
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create artwork celebrating community helpers they've learned about

opening.activity: Art inspiration circle where students choose their favorite community helper to draw. Practice art vocabulary with creative gestures and artistic appreciation expressions.
opening.visualSupports: Artistic creation gestures, helper appreciation expressions, creative celebration motions

main.activity: Community helper artwork creation using various art supplies and reference photos. Students create detailed drawings or paintings of chosen helpers, including tools, uniforms, and community settings, with focus on showing appreciation.
main.visualSupports: Artistic demonstration techniques, detailed observation gestures, creative expression encouragement

decisionPoints.question: Should students choose their favorite helper or draw multiple helpers?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Allow choice of favorite helper to ensure personal connection and artistic motivation
decisionPoints.ifNo: Assign specific helpers to ensure variety across classroom while allowing artistic interpretation

decisionPoints.question: What art materials will help students best express their appreciation?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide variety of materials so students can choose tools that match their artistic vision
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use consistent art materials to focus on content creation rather than material choice

closing.activity: Artist appreciation circle where students share their helper artwork and practice describing with 'J'ai dessiné... parce que...'

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students feeling their artwork isn't good enough to show appreciation
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize that thoughtful effort shows appreciation, focus on helper recognition rather than artistic perfection

lessons.realWorldConnection: Creating art about community helpers helps us remember and appreciate their important work

lessons.title: Jeu de rôles: Nous sommes des aides communautaires
lessons.oneGoal: Students will role-play being different community helpers to practice helper vocabulary and actions

opening.activity: Role-play preparation circle where students choose community helper roles and practice helper-specific vocabulary and actions. Review respectful role-play guidelines.
opening.visualSupports: Helper-specific gestures and movements, role-play demonstration techniques, respectful performance expressions

main.activity: Community helper role-play scenarios where students act out helper roles, interact with community members, and demonstrate helper services. Include appreciation interactions between helpers and community members.
main.visualSupports: Role-specific actions and movements, community interaction demonstrations, helper service expressions

decisionPoints.question: Which helper roles are most engaging and appropriate for Grade 1 role-play?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on active, visible helpers like firefighters, teachers, store workers, safety helpers
decisionPoints.ifNo: Include variety of helpers and let students explore different roles throughout activity

decisionPoints.question: Should students choose their own roles or rotate through different helpers?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Allow role choice to ensure engagement while encouraging some role rotation for variety
decisionPoints.ifNo: Assign roles to ensure variety and give all students opportunity to explore different helpers

closing.activity: Role-play reflection circle where students share what they learned about helpers through acting and practice saying 'Maintenant je comprends que...'

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students becoming too silly or losing educational focus during role-play
troubleshooting.then: Use structured scenarios, frequent appreciation reminders, and clear performance expectations to maintain educational purpose

lessons.realWorldConnection: Playing community helper roles helps us understand what different helpers do every day

lessons.title: Lettres de remerciement aux aides communautaires
lessons.oneGoal: Students will write simple thank you letters to community helpers expressing appreciation

opening.activity: Letter writing circle where students practice gratitude vocabulary and choose community helpers to thank. Review letter writing basics and appreciation expressions.
opening.visualSupports: Letter writing gestures, gratitude expressions, appreciation demonstration techniques

main.activity: Thank you letter creation using simple templates and guided writing support. Students write or dictate letters to specific community helpers, including drawings and expressing specific appreciation for helper contributions to community.
main.visualSupports: Writing demonstration techniques, gratitude expression examples, letter completion celebrations

decisionPoints.question: Which community helpers should receive student thank you letters?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Target helpers students have met or observed, like school helpers, local store workers, safety helpers
decisionPoints.ifNo: Choose variety of helpers to represent different types of community service students have learned about

decisionPoints.question: What writing level is appropriate for Grade 1 thank you letters?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Support simple sentences, drawings, and dictated messages that express genuine appreciation
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide templates with starter phrases that students can complete with specific appreciation details

closing.activity: Letter sharing circle where students share portions of their letters and practice saying 'J'ai écrit pour remercier...'

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students struggling to express specific appreciation in letters
troubleshooting.then: Provide sentence starters, specific appreciation examples, and drawing options to supplement written expression

lessons.realWorldConnection: Thanking community helpers shows appreciation and builds positive community relationships

lessons.title: Célébration des aides communautaires
lessons.oneGoal: Students will plan and participate in a celebration honoring all types of community helpers

opening.activity: Celebration planning circle where students share ideas for honoring community helpers. Practice celebration vocabulary with festive gestures and appreciation expressions.
opening.visualSupports: Celebration gestures (clapping, cheering), planning motions, community appreciation expressions

main.activity: Community helper celebration preparation including decoration making, appreciation speech practice, and gratitude expression preparation. Students create celebration elements that honor different types of helpers learned throughout unit.
main.visualSupports: Celebration preparation actions, appreciation demonstration techniques, festive community expressions

decisionPoints.question: Should we invite real community helpers to our celebration?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Invite available local helpers to attend and receive student appreciation in person
decisionPoints.ifNo: Create celebration that honors helpers symbolically and prepares students to express appreciation in community

decisionPoints.question: What type of celebration activities would best honor community helpers?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include appreciation speeches, thank you art displays, helper role demonstrations, and gratitude expressions
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on student-led appreciation activities that demonstrate learning and genuine gratitude

closing.activity: Celebration reflection circle where students share their favorite part of honoring helpers and practice saying 'Nous célébrons nos héros communautaires!'

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students becoming too excited and losing focus on helper appreciation purpose
troubleshooting.then: Use structured celebration activities, frequent appreciation reminders, and clear expectations for respectful celebration

lessons.realWorldConnection: Celebrating community helpers together shows our gratitude and builds community connections

lessons.title: Nous faisons partie de notre communauté automnale
lessons.oneGoal: Students will reflect on their learning and understand their important place in the autumn community

opening.activity: Community belonging circle where students reflect on all the helpers they've learned about and how they feel as community members. Practice belonging vocabulary with inclusive gestures.
opening.visualSupports: Inclusive community gestures, belonging expressions, proud community member demonstrations

main.activity: Community learning reflection using unit review materials and personal growth assessment. Students create a 'My Community Learning' book showing their favorite helpers, how they want to contribute, and their pride in community belonging.
main.visualSupports: Reflection demonstration techniques, learning celebration gestures, community pride expressions

decisionPoints.question: How do we help students articulate what they've learned about community?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use specific prompts about favorite helpers, most interesting discoveries, and personal community connections
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide sentence starters and visual prompts to help students express learning and community understanding

decisionPoints.question: Should reflection focus on helper appreciation or student community belonging?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Balance both helper appreciation and student recognition of their own community membership and contribution potential
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus primarily on student community belonging while acknowledging helper learning throughout unit

closing.activity: Community pride circle where students share one thing they're proud to know about their community and practice saying 'Je suis fier de faire partie de ma communauté!'

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students not feeling confident about their place in community
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize that all community members are important, highlight student contributions, and celebrate community belonging

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding our community helps us feel proud to belong and excited to contribute as we grow

familyConnections.unitLetter:
Chers parents et familles,

Nous sommes ravis de commencer notre nouvelle unité: ""

Cette unité permettra à votre enfant de:
• Explorer des concepts importants en sciences humaines
• Développer du vocabulaire en français
• Pratiquer de nouvelles compétences
• Faire des connexions avec la vie quotidienne

Quelques thèmes que nous explorerons:
Notre école dans la communauté, Les personnes qui nous aident à l'école, Les changements d'automne dans notre communauté, Les gens qui nous gardent en sécurité, Visite d'un pompier à l'école

Comment vous pouvez aider à la maison:
• Demandez à votre enfant de partager ce qu'il/elle a appris
• Pratiquez le nouveau vocabulaire ensemble (voir la liste ci-jointe)
• Essayez les activités suggérées quand vous avez du temps
• Célébrez les efforts et les progrès, pas seulement les résultats

Partagez vos traditions familiales et culturelles avec votre enfant.

N'hésitez pas à me contacter si vous avez des questions ou si vous souhaitez partager des ressources culturelles liées à cette unité.

Chaque famille a des histoires importantes à partager!

Cordialement,
[Nom de l'enseignant(e)]
